criteria.change: Add normalise-in/normalise-out pairs beside n-dynamic-lane and n-bitcast-lanes for the two new witnesses. Show getelementptr i8,p,3 for the second i24 lane and a zext i1-to-i2 before comparing against 2; retain the existing i32-index expectations [5,9,0,0] for indices [0,1,2,-1].

blocking.problem: The ordinary vector-memory rule says "getelementptr T, ptr p, i64 k" followed by load T, and exempts only integer lanes whose width is not a multiple of 8. Scalar allocation stride can exceed lane width even when that width is a multiple of 8. Witness: target datalayout="e-p:64:64-i64:64-i24:32-n8:16:32:64-S128"; @bytes is an eight-byte constant containing 01 02 03 04 05 06 07 08; load <2 x i24>,ptr @bytes,align 1; extractelement lane 1. The vector lane starts at byte 3, so its value is 0x060504=394500. The prescribed getelementptr i24,@bytes,1 advances four bytes and returns 0x070605=460293. opt-18 and opt-23 both verify the original and explicit replacement and constant-fold them to these different results. Replacing that GEP with getelementptr i8,@bytes,3 gives 394500 on both. The same mistake affects stores and can turn an otherwise valid vector access into an out-of-allocation fault. This is a wrong defined computation, not an encoding choice; the existing packed-i1 exception does not cover it.
blocking.fix: In §12.6 replace the vector-memory bullet with: "Lay out every vector load/store according to the vector type’s datalayout bit string, without inserting scalar allocation padding between lanes. Lane k starts at bit k*bitwidth(T). Scalar GEP T is permitted only when its allocation stride equals that lane spacing; otherwise use byte offsets or packed-byte extraction/insertion. The replacement accesses only the original vector storage range, derives each scalar alignment from the original alignment and its actual byte offset, and preserves inactive bits for masked operations." A second viable implementation is a packed integer load/store plus lane extraction/insertion for every vector, followed by N22 legalization; I would retain the scalar fast path when the equality holds. Add a checked i24 pair using offsets 0 and 3 with align 1: the byte witness above must return 394500/code 0, and the matching vector store must write its two three-byte lane values contiguously.

blocking.problem: N15 specifies "%nz.c.r = icmp uge iK i, L" without ensuring that L fits in iK. LLVM permits an index narrower than the vector length. Witness: define i8 @f(i1 %i) { %r = extractelement <2 x i8> <i8 5,i8 9>, i1 %i; ret i8 %r }. Both possible indices are valid and return 5 and 9. N15 emits icmp uge i1 %i,2; LLVM parses the i1 constant as zero, so the guard is always true and the prescribed select returns zero for both inputs. opt-18 and opt-23 verify this rewrite and fold it to ret i8 0; direct constant-index probes return 5 and 9. A zext to i2 before the comparison removes the erroneous guard on both majors. Insertion similarly becomes an unintended no-op. N21 lane comparisons can also alias unreachable lane numbers if those constants are truncated back to the narrow index type.
blocking.fix: In §12.2 N15 state: "Interpret the index as an unsigned integer. Perform the comparison with L in width W=max(K,ceil(log2(L+1))), zero-extending the index when W>K; the constant L must be represented exactly. Alternatively, when every iK value is below L, fold the out-of-range predicate to false." In §12.6 state: "Dynamic lane-selection comparisons use that same widened index and exact lane constants, or omit lanes unrepresentable by the original unsigned index; lane constants must never wrap." I would use the widened comparison uniformly. Add the i1 witness: zext i1 %i to i2; icmp uge i2 %wide,2; extract returns 5 for 0 and 9 for 1. An insertion of 7 must produce [7,9] for 0 and [5,7] for 1. Keep n-dynamic-lane’s i32 indices 2 and -1 returning zero.

previous_status.note: TDL-7/10 and §18.2 require successful-return cleanup of flags and trajectory workspace; the count-0/2 identity witness now requires P(c=1)=0.
§§17.3 and 16.4 now require logical allocation checks even for non-coh shadow-stack accesses, and §8.5 replays that metadata; the popped-frame load faults 7 before access.
§§6.1/6.3/6.5 distinguish fresh allocation identities from reusable slots and validate generation plus liveness, so a stale handle traps T-DEAD despite N(s)=1.
Loop control records are no longer leak-exempt outputs; successful forward and standalone-adjoint returns must clean them, preserving the count-0/1 X;X interference witness.
§18.2 fixes latest-before-first-reversed-consumer placement, unused-record placement, ties and producer lifetimes; H(a),record(a),CX(record,t) gives the specified plus-input result.
§§8.2/8.6/16.2 define a single W_empty call with a hidden clean target and ordinary charging/fault behavior; discarded returns do not create payload or remove execution.

TDL-10/§18.2 require a bounded inverse for standalone overwritten-guard bijections; noninjective B2 uses the existing compute/out-of-place distinction, with compute(B2,empty) restoring all three entry states.
The deterministic §18.2 deferred-record scheduler removes the placement ambiguity; the zero-input/final-H probe now has probabilities 1/2 and 1/2.
TDL-2/11 and §18.2 consistently retain coverage for permitted CC stores to covered bytes while invalidating it for event writes; observe/store9/observe ends Cl and returns 9.

§6.5 now includes may-ancestor setjmp continuations and defines E(c) on the augmented recurrence; the interprocedural witness is BLK-1 with two distinct live fallback slots, also inherited by R hoisting.

path_to_accept: 1. Correct §12.6 vector memory layout for padded scalar element types and add the i24 load/store witness with lane-1 value 394500. 2. Correct N15 and N21 dynamic lane comparisons so L and lane numbers cannot truncate in narrow index types; add i1 extract/insert witnesses returning [5,9] and the stated inserted vectors. Execute these original/replacement pairs on the supported LLVM majors and keep the existing round-3 witnesses passing. These are the only acceptance-blocking changes; no ISA extension or new proof machinery is needed.
summary: All ten previous blockers are resolved: SOL-R3-01, SOL-R3-02, SOL-R3-03, R3-CODEX-01, R3-CODEX-02, R3-CODEX-03, BD3-R3-1, BD3-R3-2, BD3-R3-3 and BD3-R3-4. Both previous loop-history regressions are also repaired, and I found no new regression introduced by the round-4 diff. I reviewed the complete embedded snapshot and confirmed the fixes before checking new cases. Two previously unreported core normalization errors remain: padded vector lane addressing and narrow vector-index bounds checks. Independent headless LLVM 18/23 probes reproduce both and their corrected results. The review therefore requests revision for these two S0 findings; the supplied full-checker receipt is not represented as a fresh run.
